messages.content: I need to start putting together our New York school-break trip. It will be the three of us, Friday, February 13 through Wednesday, February 18. Our daughter cannot leave school early Friday, and she needs to be back for school Thursday morning.
I can compare the flights, airport transfers, and five-night hotel cost together. What time can you realistically reach DFW Friday, and where are the two scheduled activities in Manhattan?

We can be at DFW by 5:15 p.m. if we leave directly from school. We have a 2:00 p.m. matinee Saturday in the Theater District, and a youth-arts program Tuesday at 10:00 a.m. near Grand Central. Those two things are fixed.

That makes departures from about 6:15 p.m. onward workable, although anything before 6:45 would leave little margin for parking and security. For the return, should I protect Wednesday daytime for sightseeing, or is getting home earlier more important? Also, do you want one room for all three?

One room for all three. I would rather not leave Manhattan at dawn Wednesday. A midafternoon flight home would be fine, and I want to see the actual total difference between LaGuardia and JFK, not just whichever airfare looks cheaper.

I found two useful nonstop patterns at current quoted prices. The LaGuardia option leaves DFW Friday at 6:45 p.m. and arrives LGA at 11:04 p.m.; Wednesday it leaves LGA at 3:40 p.m. and reaches DFW at 6:43 p.m. The fare is $549 per person, or $1,647 for three. The JFK option leaves at 7:30 p.m. and arrives at 11:58 p.m.; the return departs at 4:35 p.m. and arrives at 7:49 p.m. It is $463 per person, or $1,389 for three. Both quotes include a standard carry-on per traveler but no checked bags.
The JFK fare is $258 less, but I assume the ride is worse that late. What should I budget door to door? We will probably use a car rather than haul luggage onto trains close to midnight.

For LaGuardia to Midtown late Friday, I would allow 35 to 60 minutes and budget about $65 to $85 including tolls and tip. The Wednesday ride back is commonly 40 to 70 minutes; another $65 to $80 is reasonable. Using $150 round trip gives the LGA flight-and-transfer subtotal of about $1,797. From JFK, allow roughly 55 to 90 minutes Friday and 60 to 95 minutes Wednesday. A taxi or car generally lands around $100 to $120 each way after surcharges, tolls, and tip, so a $220 allowance makes that subtotal about $1,609. JFK still saves approximately $188, but it adds about 40 to 70 minutes of total ground travel and gets you to the hotel close to 1:15 a.m. if traffic and baggage pickup cooperate.
That is helpful. Keep both in view for now, but the LaGuardia schedule sounds easier. What hotel areas make sense for both events without paying the absolute top Times Square rates?

The practical band is from the west side of Midtown down into north Chelsea. Staying near Bryant Park or Times Square minimizes Saturday walking and keeps Tuesday's Grand Central trip simple. Chelsea can lower the room cost, but you would use the subway or a car for both fixed events. I found a central candidate and a lower-cost Chelsea candidate with rooms that accommodate three without relying on a rollaway.
Show me those. Please be specific about the beds, because a king room marketed for three will not work for us.

Candidate one is the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central, in a room with two queen beds. The current five-night price is $1,925 before mandatory taxes and fees and $2,248 estimated all-in. It is about a 5- to 12-minute walk to many Theater District venues and roughly 15 minutes on foot to Grand Central. Candidate two is Hyatt Place New York/Chelsea, also quoted with two queen beds. Its five-night total is $1,742 before taxes and mandatory charges, or $2,036 all-in. From there, allow about 20 to 25 minutes by subway or 20 to 35 minutes by car to either activity. Neither quote includes parking, which you do not need here.
Does either include breakfast? And are those totals for all three of us, not per person?

Yes, each hotel total covers one room for all three guests for five nights. The Hyatt Place rate includes breakfast for registered guests. The Hilton Garden Inn rate does not; breakfast is available for purchase. Wi-Fi is included at both. The quoted room categories explicitly list two queen beds, though the final booking page should still be checked before payment because New York inventory changes quickly.
Can you put the four flight-and-hotel combinations side by side with transfers? Leave meals and the two activities out, but include anything else that is mandatory in the quotes.

Using the all-in room prices and the car-transfer allowances: LGA plus Hilton Garden Inn is about $4,045 ($1,647 flights + $150 transfers + $2,248 hotel). LGA plus Hyatt Place Chelsea is about $3,833 ($1,647 + $150 + $2,036). JFK plus Hilton Garden Inn is about $3,857 ($1,389 + $220 + $2,248). JFK plus Hyatt Place Chelsea is about $3,645 ($1,389 + $220 + $2,036). These estimates include the mandatory hotel charges shown and airport transportation, but exclude meals, activities, optional hotel incidentals, and any checked-bag fees.
Interesting. So the central hotel with JFK is only $24 more than Chelsea with LaGuardia.

Correct based on these quotes: $3,857 versus $3,833. That trade is essentially a wash financially. JFK plus the central hotel gives you easier movement during the stay but the longest arrival night. LGA plus Chelsea gives you the cleaner airport schedule, included breakfast, and a longer commute to both fixed activities.
For Saturday, how risky is that late Friday arrival? We do not have anything before the 2:00 matinee, but I do not want one flight delay to wreck the weekend.

Either Friday flight leaves substantial recovery time before 2:00 p.m. Saturday, but the LGA option is the stronger schedule. It departs 45 minutes earlier, lands 54 minutes earlier, and has a shorter transfer. Under normal operations you would reach a Midtown hotel around midnight to 12:30 a.m.; with JFK, approximately 1:00 to 1:30 a.m. A cancellation would be the larger risk with either last-evening pattern, so before ticketing I would check whether the airline has a later same-night flight and what Saturday-morning reaccommodation options exist.
Agreed. I am leaning toward LaGuardia. Is 3:40 Wednesday late enough that we are not wasting the whole day, and early enough that a delay should still get us home before Thursday school?

It is a reasonable balance. You could have breakfast, check out, and keep luggage with the hotel, then leave Midtown around 12:45 to 1:00 p.m. for LGA. The scheduled 6:43 p.m. arrival gives you a meaningful buffer before Thursday morning. It does not eliminate disruption risk, but it is materially better for the school deadline than the JFK flight arriving at 7:49 p.m.

Then narrow it to that LaGuardia schedule and the two hotels. I am not ready to buy today. Before we do, I will need the cancellation terms for both rooms and the flight fare rules, plus a check that the two-queen inventory is really there.

The working shortlist is now the nonstop DFW-LGA itinerary departing Friday, February 13 at 6:45 p.m. and returning Wednesday, February 18 at 3:40 p.m., quoted at $1,647 for three. The lodging finalists are Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central at an estimated $2,248 all-in and Hyatt Place New York/Chelsea at an estimated $2,036 all-in with breakfast. Including a $150 round-trip car allowance, the estimated totals are $4,045 and $3,833 respectively. Nothing has been booked. The next step is to reprice the itinerary, verify fare and cancellation rules, confirm the exact two-queen room inventory and occupancy for three, and review each hotel's cancellation deadline before any purchase.
